title: GitHub Copilot operating card
summary: This correction record helps an intermediate practitioner decide whether the operating card has enough verified evidence to use. Product-specific operating instructions remain UNKNOWN and are omitted until the original resource and its citation history can be reviewed.
prerequisites: The verbatim previous version of the resource
The previous external citation record and any replacement URL
Access to the current first-party GitHub documentation

sections.title: Can an intermediate practitioner use this operating card now?
paragraphs: No. This resource is written for an intermediate practitioner, but its previous operating instructions, configuration details, procedures, and expected evidence are UNKNOWN because the existing resource was not supplied for review. Those details are omitted rather than presented as verified guidance.

GitHub describes GitHub Copilot as an AI coding assistant. No more specific feature, interface, version, configuration key, or operating procedure is asserted here because the supplied material does not establish one.
sections.callout: Do not reconstruct missing operating instructions from memory. Obtain the previous resource and verify each affected claim against directly accessible first-party documentation before use.

sections.title: Source correction and remediation path
paragraphs: The citation record that changed is content/resources/coding-tools/github-copilot-operating-card.json. It was recorded as an unregistered publisher, was never verified, and is a repository-relative path rather than an HTTPS external source. No evidence establishes that a particular external source moved. The affected product claims are therefore UNKNOWN and omitted.

Step 1. Obtain a verbatim copy of the previous JSON resource so its wording, section identifiers, procedures, and citation mapping can be compared. If the previous file cannot be obtained, stop the correction and request it from the repository owner rather than drafting a replacement.

Step 2. Identify the previous external citation, any redirect or replacement, its prior verification date, and the claims that depended on it. If that citation history cannot be established, mark the affected claims UNKNOWN and omit them until evidence is available.

Step 3. Open the applicable first-party GitHub documentation and verify only the affected claims. If a page does not resolve directly over HTTPS or its applicability is unclear, do not retain the dependent instruction; request a resolvable first-party source or editorial review.

Step 4. Apply only the correction supported by the comparison. If the baseline is unavailable or the affected scope cannot be isolated, do not publish a supposed minimal-diff update because preservation of unaffected material cannot be demonstrated.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence consists of the verbatim previous resource, the old and replacement citation records, successful access to each retained HTTPS source, a mapping from changed source content to affected claims, and a diff limited to those claims.

Verify the correction by parsing the committed file as one JSON object, confirming that its filename without the .json extension equals both id and slug, checking identifier uniqueness against the complete catalogue, and reviewing the diff against the previous file. If parsing fails, remove any text outside the object and correct the invalid JSON before retrying. If the filename, identifiers, or catalogue uniqueness cannot be confirmed, stop publication and obtain the target path or catalogue registry.

The required minimal-diff verification is currently UNKNOWN because the previous resource and catalogue registry were not supplied. The product guidance must remain unpublished until those inputs are available.
